provenance.sourcePolicy: External behavior oracle only; source and assets are neither committed nor packaged.

behaviors.observation: The root and unknown routes present a landing state with a start action.
The start action enters the single playable level.
A loading overlay precedes the playable level.
A frame statistics panel is present during play.
Play shows a centered crosshair and bottom weapon overlay.
A user gesture requests pointer lock and unlocks background audio.
Mouse movement changes view direction while pointer lock is active.
WASD moves relative to view and diagonal movement is normalized.
Movement advances by 0.09 world units per fixed simulation update at player height 1.
Walls, the blocking prop, and enemy bodies prevent movement within the observed radius.
Space press or hold fires no faster than every 650ms and retains one player projectile.
The firing weapon animation lasts 350ms.
A projectile spawns one unit along view, advances 0.8 units per update, and disappears near walls or enemies.
The level starts with five one-hit enemies.
Idle enemies billboard and wander, reconsidering direction after three seconds.
Enemies aggro within 15 units when grid line-of-sight is clear and stop advancing within 2 units.

evidence.target: enemy aggro and line of sight

behaviors.observation: Aggro enemies fire no faster than every 1000ms and enemy projectiles collide with walls or the player.
Enemy hits have no player-health, damage, death, or game-over consequence.
One player hit kills an enemy, plays death feedback, animates for 1000ms, then leaves a collidable corpse.
The level starts with eleven collectibles.
A collectible within one unit plays feedback and disappears.
Collecting another item can restore a previously collected item; this oracle quirk remains explicit.
Enemy, collectible, decorative, weapon, and death visuals animate with pixel-art filtering.
Background, firing, collection, and death each have audible state; every projectile uses firing feedback at volume 0.5.
Escape unlocks aim without pausing simulation or keyboard movement.
Browser back exits to landing; re-entry resets level actors and player state.
The oracle has no win condition, score, health, ammo, touch controls, pause, reset, or in-game exit control.
Rejected pointer-lock or audio attempts remain recoverable through another user gesture.
WebGL unavailability exposes an actionable application failure rather than a false playable state.
Route exit and unmount do not leave duplicate listeners, frames, audio, or stale input on re-entry.

constructs.evidence: TSRX components and Octane hooks preserve the observable application lifecycle.
Public @octanejs/three Canvas, frame, camera, event, scene, material, and geometry APIs own the renderer behavior.
Public @octanejs/drei Stats, Instance, and Instances exports are consumed by the WebGL scene. The loading shell is app-owned because Loader depends on client-only renderer progress during SSR.
Application state uses public Octane hooks; no compatibility shim is embedded in the game.
Compiler-owned hook slots and renderer-specific .three.tsrx modules are structural only and preserve the behavior contract.
